root_cause.text: The error handling path in sd_probe() fails to release the gendisk reference when device_add(&sdkp->disk_dev) fails, causing a resource leak because put_device() only frees the scsi_disk structure but not the associated gendisk.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `put_disk(gd);` immediately after `put_device(&sdkp->disk_dev);` in the device_add() error path. The commit message explicitly states that "put_device() runs scsi_disk_release(), which frees the scsi_disk but leaves the gendisk referenced," and notes that the device_add_disk() error path already calls put_disk(gd), establishing that this cleanup was missing from the device_add() error path and needs to mirror that existing cleanup pattern.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix resource leak by releasing disk object on device_add() failure in sd_probe().
intent_record.what: Added a `put_disk(gd);` call in the error handling path of sd_probe() after device_add() fails, before the goto out statement.
intent_record.how: When device_add() fails, the code now properly releases the disk object referenced by `gd` in addition to the device reference. This prevents a resource leak where the disk structure would not be freed if device registration failed.

grouping_result.intent: Fix resource leak by releasing disk object on device_add() failure in sd_probe().

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the vulnerability root cause by fixing the resource leak in sd_probe(). The root cause identifies that gendisk reference is not released when device_add(&sdkp->disk_dev) fails, and this group's core intent is to release the disk object on device_add() failure, which is the exact fix needed to resolve the leak.

candidates.rationale: This statement is insufficient to handle the resource leak. When device_add() fails, put_device() only decrements the reference count of the scsi_disk device structure but does not release the associated gendisk object. The gendisk reference acquired earlier needs to be explicitly released via put_disk() to prevent the resource leak.

The error handling path jumps to 'out' label without releasing the gendisk reference. This causes the code to skip the necessary cleanup of the disk object that was allocated and referenced before the device_add() call, resulting in a resource leak.

The vulnerability root cause describes a resource leak where put_device() fails to release the gendisk reference when device_add() fails. The error handling logic at line 3539 ('put_device(&sdkp->disk_dev)') remains unchanged in substance from the original code (which had 'put_device(&sdkp->dev)'). The underlying issue (if it exists) would have been present before this commit and remains present after it. Since the vulnerable construct (inadequate error handling in device_add failure path) is not introduced by this commit, has_bug=false.

Author: Ming Lei <ming.lei@redhat.com>

    scsi: sd: Free scsi_disk device via put_device()
    
    After a device is initialized via device_initialize() it should be freed
    via put_device(). sd_probe() currently gets this wrong, fix it up.
    
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20210906090112.531442-1-ming.lei@redhat.com
    Reviewed-by: Bart Van Assche <bvanassche@acm.org>

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit shows the fix being applied to the vulnerability. The root cause was that when device_add(&sdkp->dev) fails, the gendisk reference was not being released. The fix demonstrates: (1) Moving get_device(dev) earlier to line 3404 where sdkp->dev.parent is assigned, ensuring proper reference counting; (2) Adding put_device(&sdkp->dev) in the error path at line 3410 when device_add() fails, which properly releases the device reference; (3) Changing the error goto from 'out_free_index' to 'out', ensuring proper cleanup. The vulnerable construct (missing put_device() on device_add() failure) is being fixed in this commit, not introduced. This is a Bug-Fixing Commit, not a Bug-Introducing Commit.
